problem: Which of the following is a factor of ${u}^{2}-2u+5?$
worked_solution:
First, we let $f(u)={u}^{2}-2u+5.$

Next, we solve $f(u)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-2u+5 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2\cdot u+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+5 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =-4 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-1)^{2} & =(2\text{i})^{2} \\ u-1 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ u & =1\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${u}_{1}=1+2\text{i}$ and ${u}_{2}=1-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression ${u}^{2}-2u+5$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2u+5 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(1+2\text{i}))(u-(1-2\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $u-(1-2\text{i})$ is a factor of ${u}^{2}-2u+5.$
